1 Purpose
1.1 This procedure describes how a branch opens a savings account for an individual customer.

4.1 The branch officer assigns a risk rating of low, medium or high.

4.3 High-risk applications are referred to the Branch Manager.

1 Purpose
1.1 This procedure protects workers from the unexpected start-up of machinery during servicing and maintenance.
2 Procedure
2.1The authorized employee notifies all affected employees that the machine will be shut down.
2.2 The machine is shut down using its normal stopping procedure.
2.3All energy sources (electrical, pneumatic, hydraulic) are isolated.
2.4 The authorized employee applies a personal lock and tag to every energy-isolating device.
2.5The authorized employee verifies zero energy by attempting to start the machine.
2.6Maintenance or servicing is performed.
2.7Verification of zero energy must always be performed before any maintenance or servicing begins.
3 Exceptions
3.1 For minor tool changes expected to take less than 10 minutes, the operator may proceed directly to maintenance after shutting down the machine.
4 Restoring equipment
4.1 After maintenance, the authorized employee removes tools, ensures all employees are clear, and removes their lock and tag.
4.2Only the employee who applied a lock may remove it.
4.3Equipment must be returned to service as soon as possible.

Appendix A to § 1910.147—Typical Minimal Lockout Procedure
General

The following simple lockout procedure is provided to assist employers in developing their procedures so they meet the requirements of this standard. When the energy isolating devices are not lockable, tagout may be used, provided the employer complies with the provisions of the standard which require additional training and more rigorous periodic inspections. When tagout is used and the energy isolating devices are lockable, the employer must provide full employee protection (see paragraph (c)(3)) and additional training and more rigorous periodic inspections are required. For more complex systems, more comprehensive procedures may need to be developed, documented and utilized.
Lockout Procedure
Lockout procedure for
(Name of Company for single procedure or identification of equipment if multiple procedures are used)
Purpose

This procedure establishes the minimum requirements for the lockout of energy isolating devices whenever maintenance or servicing is done on machines or equipment. It shall be used to ensure that the machine or equipment is stopped, isolated from all potentially hazardous energy sources and locked out before employees perform any servicing or maintenance where the unexpected energization or start-up of the machine or equipment or release of stored energy could cause injury.
Compliance With This Program

All employees are required to comply with the restrictions and limitations imposed upon them during the use of lockout. The authorized employees are required to perform the lockout in accordance with this procedure. All employees, upon observing a machine or piece of equipment which is locked out to perform servicing or maintenance shall not attempt to start, energize or use that machine or equipment.
Type of compliance enforcement to be taken for violation of the above.
Sequence of Lockout

(1) Notify all affected employees that servicing or maintenance is required on a machine or equipment and that the machine or equipment must be shut down and locked out to perform the servicing or maintenance.
Name(s)/Job Title(s) of affected employees and how to notify.

(2) The authorized employee shall refer to the company procedure to identify the type and magnitude of the energy that the machine or equipment utilizes, shall understand the hazards of the energy, and shall know the methods to control the energy.
Type(s) and magnitude(s) of energy, its hazards and the methods to control the energy.
(3) If the machine or equipment is operating, shut it down by the normal stopping procedure (depress stop button, open switch, close valve, etc.).
Type(s) and location(s) of machine or equipment operating controls.
(4) De-activate the energy isolating device(s) so that the machine or equipment is isolated from the energy source(s).
Type(s) and location(s) of energy isolating devices.
(5) Lock out the energy isolating device(s) with assigned individual lock(s).

(6) Stored or residual energy (such as that in capacitors, springs, elevated machine members, rotating flywheels, hydraulic systems, and air, gas, steam, or water pressure, etc.) must be dissipated or restrained by methods such as grounding, repositioning, blocking, bleeding down, etc.
Type(s) of stored energy—methods to dissipate or restrain.

(7) Ensure that the equipment is disconnected from the energy source(s) by first checking that no personnel are exposed, then verify the isolation of the equipment by operating the push button or other normal operating control(s) or by testing to make certain the equipment will not operate.
Caution: Return operating control(s) to neutral or “off” position after verifying the isolation of the equipment.
Method of verifying the isolation of the equipment.
(8) The machine or equipment is now locked out.
Restoring Equipment to Service. When the servicing or maintenance is completed and the machine or equipment is ready to return to normal operating condition, the following steps shall be taken.

(1) Check the machine or equipment and the immediate area around the machine or equipment to ensure that nonessential items have been removed and that the machine or equipment components are operationally intact.
(2) Check the work area to ensure that all employees have been safely positioned or removed from the area.
(3) Verify that the controls are in neutral.
(4) Remove the lockout devices and reenergize the machine or equipment.
Note:
The removal of some forms of blocking may require reenergization of the machine before safe removal.
(5) Notify affected employees that the servicing or maintenance is completed and the machine or equipment is ready for use.

Title: Travel Voucher Preparation Process for Invitational Travelers
SOP Number: DTT-CO-4
Version Number/Date: No. 1
Supersedes: N/A
Effective Date: February 7, 2019
Review Date: February 7, 2019
BACKGROUND

The National Technical Training Program (NTTP) provides technical assistance to the States, Tribes and Federal personnel by enhancing the technical skills of reclamation and regulatory staff. Technical Assistance is achieved by offering specialized on-demand courses to assist the States, Tribes and Personnel in the successful implementation of both Titles IV and V of SMCRA. Course Coordinators provide logistical, administrative and customer service support to accomplish this mission.
PURPOSE

The purpose of this SOP is to provide standardized procedures for preparing and processing travel voucher for invitational travelers attending NTTP training sessions. Invitational travelers who require reimbursement for travel expenses on travel that required lodging must follow the below procedures.
SCOPE
The scope of this SOP is not limited to NTTP.
RESPONSIBILITY

NTTP coordinators are responsible for the implementation of this process. Instructors are responsible for reviewing these procedures with travelers on the last day of class. Invitational travelers are responsible for providing all needed information to NTTP coordinators.
PROCEDURES
Invitational travelers must provide all travel receipts/information to the assigned coordinator one business day after completing a course.

Upon receipt of all needed travel receipts/information, the assigned coordinator will create the invitational traveler's travel voucher in the travel management system (Concur) within one business day.
After creating the travel voucher in Concur, the assigned coordinator will send the completed travel voucher to the invitational traveler for signature.
Invitational travelers must review, sign, date, and return their completed travel voucher to the assigned coordinator within one business day.
Upon receipt of the signed-completed travel voucher from the invitational traveler, the assigned coordinator will upload/attach the signed travel voucher in Concur and stamp the document "T-ENTERED".
Travel vouchers are reviewed for allowable expenses compliancy and accuracy.
All travel vouchers missing a completed travel voucher signed by the invitational traveler and/or missing documentation (travel receipts) will be "RETURNED" by Denver Finance Office.
All successfully reviewed travel vouchers must be approved in Concur by the Chief and/or the assigned approval official.
All approved travel vouchers are submitted for payment.
Invitational travelers should contact the assigned coordinator for reimbursement status.
CALCULATIONS/DATA HANDLING/DOCUMENTATION REQUIREMENTS
The data for this SOP is captured in the CONCUR. Document copies are held in NTTP files for three years and then destroyed.

items.text: 1. Purpose
This SOP defines how customer complaints are logged, investigated and resolved, including when a refund is issued.
2. Roles
Customer Service Agent (CSA): first point of contact; logs and investigates complaints.
Team Lead: supervises CSAs and reviews escalated complaints.
Finance Manager: approves high-value refunds.
Service Delivery Lead: handles complaints the Team Lead cannot resolve.
Customer Experience Champion: reviews closed complaints for recurring issues.
3. Service levels
All complaints must be resolved within 5 business days of being logged.
4. Procedure
4.1 Logging
1. The CSA shall log every complaint in the CRM within 1 business day of receipt, recording the order number and the customer's description of the problem.
2. The CSA should verify the customer's identity before discussing account details.
4.2 Investigation
3. The team will verify the order details against the order management system within 2 business days.
4. The CSA attaches the Refund Approval Form (RAF) to the complaint record and records whether the complaint is upheld.
5. If the complaint is not upheld, the CSA informs the customer of the outcome and closes the complaint.
4.3 Refund decision
6. If the complaint is upheld and a refund is due:
If the refund amount is below ₹5,000, the CSA who logged the complaint approves the refund.
If the refund amount is above ₹10,000, the Finance Manager approves the refund within 3 business days.
7. The CSA completes the Refund Approval Form (RAF) with the approved amount.
8. The CSA submits the refund to the payment gateway. If the payment gateway rejects the refund, notify IT Support.
9. The CSA responds to the customer promptly to confirm the refund and closes the complaint.
4.4 Disputes and escalation
10. If the customer disputes the resolution, return to step 3.
11. If a complaint is unresolved after 48 hours, escalate it to the Service Delivery Lead.
12. The Service Delivery Lead may send the complaint back to the Team Lead for rework.
5. References
Refund Policy RP-02 §3.2 (refund eligibility).

1 Purpose
1.1 This policy sets out how employees are reimbursed for business expenses.
2 Scope
2.1 This policy applies to all staff, managers and the Finance Head of the company.
3 Submission
3.1 The requester submits an expense claim with receipts through the expense portal. The Accounts team checks every claim for receipts.
3.2 Claims without receipts are returned to the requester, who must attach the receipts and resubmit; the claim is then checked again.
4 Approval
4.1 Claims below INR 10,000 are approved by the requester's line manager.
4.2 Claims above INR 10,000 require approval from the Finance Head.
4.3 Claims submitted by a manager are approved by the Finance Head.
4.4 The Finance Head's own claims must be approved by the Finance Head.
4.5 Approvers must decide within 3 working days of receiving a claim.
5 Payment
5.1 Approved claims are paid by the Accounts team within 5 working days.
5.2 Every claim must be reimbursed within 7 calendar days of submission.
6 Audit
6.1 Claims escalated by the Audit Committee are re-reviewed by the Internal Audit team before payment.
7 Controls
7.1 No person may approve their own claim.
7.2 Reimbursements must be processed promptly and, where appropriate, in line with company policy.

1 Purpose
1.1 This procedure describes how customer disputes on card transactions are received, investigated and resolved.
2 Scope
2.1 This procedure applies to disputes raised by retail cardholders on debit and credit card transactions.
3 Intake
3.1 The customer raises a dispute through the mobile app or the contact centre. The Disputes Officer registers the dispute in the case management system.
3.2 Disputes raised more than 120 days after the transaction date are declined.
3.3 For disputes raised within 120 days, the Disputes Officer requests supporting evidence from the customer.
4 Evidence review
4.1 If the evidence is complete, the dispute proceeds to classification.
4.2 If the evidence is incomplete, the Disputes Officer sends a reminder to the customer and reviews the evidence on file again.
5 Classification and resolution
5.1 Disputes of IDR 2,000,000 or less are resolved by the Disputes Officer with a provisional credit to the customer.
5.2 Disputes above IDR 2,000,000 are referred to the Disputes Supervisor.
5.3 Disputes classified as suspected fraud are referred to the Fraud Investigation Unit.
5.4 The Disputes Supervisor either files a chargeback with the card scheme or declines the dispute.
5.5 The Fraud Investigation Unit completes its investigation as described in Annex C.
6 Timelines
6.1 The Disputes Supervisor must decide within 10 working days of referral.
6.2 Chargebacks are filed with the card scheme within 5 working days of the Supervisor's decision.
6.3 Every dispute must be resolved within 14 calendar days of registration.
7 Customer communication
7.1 The customer is informed of the outcome in a timely manner.

1 Tujuan
1.1 Prosedur ini menjelaskan cara sanggahan nasabah atas transaksi kartu diterima, diinvestigasi, dan diselesaikan.
2 Ruang lingkup
2.1 Prosedur ini berlaku untuk sanggahan yang diajukan oleh pemegang kartu ritel atas transaksi kartu debit dan kartu kredit.
3 Penerimaan sanggahan
3.1 Nasabah mengajukan sanggahan melalui aplikasi seluler atau pusat layanan nasabah. Petugas Sanggahan mencatat sanggahan tersebut dalam sistem manajemen kasus.
3.2 Sanggahan yang diajukan lebih dari 120 hari setelah tanggal transaksi ditolak.
3.3 Untuk sanggahan yang diajukan dalam waktu 120 hari, Petugas Sanggahan meminta bukti pendukung dari nasabah.
4 Penelaahan bukti
4.1 Apabila bukti lengkap, sanggahan dilanjutkan ke tahap klasifikasi.
4.2 Apabila bukti tidak lengkap, Petugas Sanggahan mengirimkan pengingat kepada nasabah dan menelaah kembali bukti yang tersedia.
5 Klasifikasi dan penyelesaian
5.1 Sanggahan dengan nilai sampai dengan Rp2.000.000 diselesaikan oleh Petugas Sanggahan dengan memberikan kredit sementara kepada nasabah.
5.2 Sanggahan dengan nilai di atas Rp2.000.000 diteruskan kepada Supervisor Sanggahan.
5.3 Sanggahan yang diklasifikasikan sebagai dugaan penipuan (fraud) diteruskan kepada Unit Investigasi Fraud.
5.4 Supervisor Sanggahan mengajukan chargeback kepada prinsipal kartu atau menolak sanggahan.
5.5 Unit Investigasi Fraud menyelesaikan investigasi sebagaimana diatur dalam Lampiran C.
6 Batas waktu
6.1 Supervisor Sanggahan wajib memberikan keputusan dalam waktu 10 hari kerja sejak sanggahan diteruskan.
6.2 Chargeback diajukan kepada prinsipal kartu dalam waktu 5 hari kerja sejak keputusan Supervisor.
6.3 Setiap sanggahan wajib diselesaikan dalam waktu 14 hari kalender sejak dicatat.
7 Komunikasi dengan nasabah
7.1 Nasabah diberi tahu mengenai hasil penyelesaian sanggahan secara tepat waktu.

1 Purpose
1.1 This procedure protects workers from the unexpected start-up of machinery during servicing and maintenance.
2 Procedure
2.1 The authorized employee notifies all affected employees that the machine will be shut down.
2.2 The machine is shut down using its normal stopping procedure.
2.3 All energy sources (electrical, pneumatic, hydraulic) are isolated.
2.4 The authorized employee applies a personal lock and tag to every energy-isolating device.
2.5 The authorized employee verifies zero energy by attempting to start the machine.
2.6 Maintenance or servicing is performed.
2.7 Verification of zero energy must always be performed before any maintenance or servicing begins.
3 Exceptions
3.1 For minor tool changes expected to take less than 10 minutes, the operator may proceed directly to maintenance after shutting down the machine.
4 Restoring equipment
4.1 After maintenance, the authorized employee removes tools, ensures all employees are clear, and removes their lock and tag.

1 Purpose

items.text: Distribution
The controlled copy of this document is held in the Document Management System (DMS). Printed or downloaded copies are uncontrolled; check the DMS for the current version before use.
1 Purpose
1.1 This policy sets out how employees are reimbursed for business expenses.
2 Scope
2.1 This policy applies to all staff, managers and the Finance Head of the company.
3 Submission
3.1 The requester submits an expense claim with receipts through the expense portal. The Accounts team checks every claim for receipts.
3.2 Claims without receipts are returned to the requester, who must attach the receipts and resubmit; the claim is then checked again.
4 Approval
4.1 Claims up to and including INR 10,000 are approved by the requester's line manager.
4.2 Claims above INR 10,000 require approval from the Finance Head.
4.3 Claims submitted by a manager are approved by the Finance Head.
4.4 The Finance Head's own claims must be approved by the Finance Head.
4.5 Approvers must decide within 3 working days of receiving a claim.
5 Payment
5.1 Approved claims are paid by the Accounts team within 5 working days.
5.2 Every claim must be reimbursed within 7 calendar days of submission.
6 Audit
6.1 Claims escalated by the Audit Committee are re-reviewed by the Internal Audit team before payment.
7 Controls
7.1 No person may approve their own claim.
7.2 Reimbursements must be processed promptly and, where appropriate, in line with company policy.

items.text: Distribution
The controlled copy of this document is held in the Document Management System (DMS). Printed or downloaded copies are uncontrolled; check the DMS for the current version before use.
1 Purpose
1.1 This procedure protects workers from the unexpected start-up of machinery during servicing and maintenance.
2 Procedure
2.1 The authorized employee notifies all affected employees that the machine will be shut down.
2.2 The machine is shut down using its normal stopping procedure.
2.3 All energy sources (electrical, pneumatic, hydraulic) are isolated.
2.4 The authorized employee applies a personal lock and tag to every energy-isolating device.
2.5 The authorized employee verifies zero energy by attempting to start the machine.
2.6 Maintenance or servicing is performed.
2.7 Verification of zero energy must always be performed before any maintenance or servicing begins.
3 Exceptions
3.1 For minor tool changes expected to take less than 10 minutes, the operator must verify zero energy before proceeding directly to maintenance after shutting down the machine.
4 Restoring equipment
4.1 After maintenance, the authorized employee removes tools, ensures all employees are clear, and removes their lock and tag.
4.2 Only the employee who applied a lock may remove it.
4.3 Equipment must be returned to service as soon as possible.

1 Purpose
1.1 This procedure describes how a branch opens a savings account for an individual customer.
2 Eligibility
2.1 Applicants must be 18 years of age or older.
2.2 Minors aged below 10 years are not eligible to open an account. Minors aged 10 years and above may open an account jointly with a guardian, as described in Section 9.
3 Know Your Customer (KYC)
3.1 The branch officer collects proof of identity and proof of address from the applicant.
3.2 If both documents are verified, the application proceeds to risk assessment.
3.3 If either document cannot be verified, the application is rejected.
4 Risk assessment
4.1 The branch officer assigns a risk rating of low, medium or high.
4.2 Low-risk applications are approved and the account is opened.
4.3 High-risk applications are referred to the Branch Manager.
4.4 The Branch Manager approves or rejects referred applications within 2 working days.
5 Account opening
5.1 The account must be opened within 3 working days of receiving a complete application.

Lockout/Tagout Procedure for Machine Maintenance

LOTO-003 · Version 2.1 · Standard Operating Procedure

Document control

Document No. | LOTO-003 | Version | 2.1
Status | Approved - Effective | Classification | Internal - Safety Critical
Effective date | 01-Sep-2026 | Next review date | 31-Aug-2027
Document owner | Plant Director | Supersedes | v2.0 dated 10-May-2025
Department | Engineering & Maintenance / EHS

Review and approval

Role | Name | Designation | Date | Signature
Prepared by | Daisuke Ito | Maintenance Supervisor | 14-Aug-2026 | e-signed (DMS)
Reviewed by | Yui Sato | Site HSE Manager | 21-Aug-2026 | e-signed (DMS)
Approved by | Takeshi Morimoto | Plant Director | 26-Aug-2026 | e-signed (DMS)

Definitions

Term | Meaning
Authorized employee | A person trained and authorized to lock or tag out machines in order to service them.
Affected employee | A person who operates or works in the area of a machine that is being serviced.
Energy-isolating device | A device that physically prevents the transmission or release of energy, such as a disconnect switch or line valve.
Zero energy state | The condition in which all energy sources are isolated and stored energy has been released.

Revision history

Version | Date | Author | Description of change
v1.0 | 03-Feb-2021 | D. Ito | Initial issue based on the corporate energy-control standard.
v2.0 | 10-May-2025 | D. Ito | Pneumatic and hydraulic energy added to clause 2.3.
v2.1 | 01-Sep-2026 | D. Ito | Section 3 added: exception for minor tool changes, at the request of Production to reduce changeover time.

Distribution

The controlled copy of this document is held in the Document Management System (DMS). Printed or downloaded copies are uncontrolled; check the DMS for the current version before use.

1 Purpose

1.1 This procedure protects workers from the unexpected start-up of machinery during servicing and maintenance.

2 Procedure

2.1 The authorized employee notifies all affected employees that the machine will be shut down.

2.2 The machine is shut down using its normal stopping procedure.

2.3 All energy sources (electrical, pneumatic, hydraulic) are isolated.

2.4 The authorized employee applies a personal lock and tag to every energy-isolating device.

2.5 The authorized employee verifies zero energy by attempting to start the machine.

2.6 Maintenance or servicing is performed.

2.7 Verification of zero energy must always be performed before any maintenance or servicing begins.

3 Exceptions

3.1 For minor tool changes expected to take less than 10 minutes, the operator may proceed directly to maintenance after shutting down the machine.

4 Restoring equipment

4.1 After maintenance, the authorized employee removes tools, ensures all employees are clear, and removes their lock and tag.

4.2 Only the employee who applied a lock may remove it.

4.3 Equipment must be returned to service as soon as possible.

ast.text:
Lockout/Tagout Procedure for Machine Maintenance

LOTO-003 · Version 2.1 · Standard Operating Procedure

Document control

Document No. | LOTO-003 | Version | 2.1
Status | Approved - Effective | Classification | Internal - Safety Critical
Effective date | 01-Sep-2026 | Next review date | 31-Aug-2027
Document owner | Plant Director | Supersedes | v2.0 dated 10-May-2025
Department | Engineering & Maintenance / EHS

Review and approval

Role | Name | Designation | Date | Signature
Prepared by | Daisuke Ito | Maintenance Supervisor | 14-Aug-2026 | e-signed (DMS)
Reviewed by | Yui Sato | Site HSE Manager | 21-Aug-2026 | e-signed (DMS)
Approved by | Takeshi Morimoto | Plant Director | 26-Aug-2026 | e-signed (DMS)

Definitions

Term | Meaning
Authorized employee | A person trained and authorized to lock or tag out machines in order to service them.
Affected employee | A person who operates or works in the area of a machine that is being serviced.
Energy-isolating device | A device that physically prevents the transmission or release of energy, such as a disconnect switch or line valve.
Zero energy state | The condition in which all energy sources are isolated and stored energy has been released.

Revision history

Version | Date | Author | Description of change
v1.0 | 03-Feb-2021 | D. Ito | Initial issue based on the corporate energy-control standard.
v2.0 | 10-May-2025 | D. Ito | Pneumatic and hydraulic energy added to clause 2.3.
v2.1 | 01-Sep-2026 | D. Ito | Section 3 added: exception for minor tool changes, at the request of Production to reduce changeover time.

Distribution

The controlled copy of this document is held in the Document Management System (DMS). Printed or downloaded copies are uncontrolled; check the DMS for the current version before use.

1 Purpose

1.1 This procedure protects workers from the unexpected start-up of machinery during servicing and maintenance.

2 Procedure

2.1 The authorized employee notifies all affected employees that the machine will be shut down.

2.2 The machine is shut down using its normal stopping procedure.

2.3 All energy sources (electrical, pneumatic, hydraulic) are isolated.

2.4 The authorized employee applies a personal lock and tag to every energy-isolating device.

2.5 The authorized employee verifies zero energy by attempting to start the machine.

2.6 Maintenance or servicing is performed.

2.7 Verification of zero energy must always be performed before any maintenance or servicing begins.

3 Exceptions

3.1 For minor tool changes expected to take less than 10 minutes, the operator must verify zero energy before proceeding directly to maintenance after shutting down the machine.

4 Restoring equipment

4.1 After maintenance, the authorized employee removes tools, ensures all employees are clear, and removes their lock and tag.

4.2 Only the employee who applied a lock may remove it.

4.3 Equipment must be returned to service as soon as possible.

Savings Account Opening Procedure

ACC-002 · Version 1.4 · Standard Operating Procedure

Document control

Document No. | ACC-002 | Version | 1.4
Status | Approved - Effective | Classification | Internal
Effective date | 15-Aug-2026 | Next review date | 14-Aug-2027
Document owner | Head - Retail Banking | Supersedes | v1.3 dated 02-Jan-2026
Department | Retail Banking - Branch Operations

Review and approval

Role | Name | Designation | Date | Signature
Prepared by | Sneha Patil | Manager - Branch Operations | 28-Jul-2026 | e-signed (DMS)
Reviewed by | Arjun Bhatt | Compliance Officer - KYC/AML | 05-Aug-2026 | e-signed (DMS)
Approved by | Meera Nair | Head - Retail Banking | 11-Aug-2026 | e-signed (DMS)

Definitions

Term | Meaning
KYC | Know Your Customer - the process of verifying the identity and address of a customer.
Branch officer | A customer service officer authorised to open accounts at a branch.
Officially valid document | A document accepted by the Bank as proof of identity or address.
Guardian | A parent or court-appointed guardian who operates the account on behalf of a minor.

Revision history

Version | Date | Author | Description of change
v1.0 | 20-Feb-2023 | S. Patil | Initial issue.
v1.3 | 02-Jan-2026 | S. Patil | Risk assessment step introduced (Section 4).
v1.4 | 15-Aug-2026 | S. Patil | Section 9 (Accounts for minors) withdrawn pending regulatory update; account opening timeline added (clause 5.1).

Distribution

The controlled copy of this document is held in the Document Management System (DMS). Printed or downloaded copies are uncontrolled; check the DMS for the current version before use.

1 Purpose

1.1 This procedure describes how a branch opens a savings account for an individual customer.

2 Eligibility

2.1 Applicants must be 18 years of age or older.

2.2 Minors aged 10 years and above may open an account jointly with a guardian, as described in Section 9.

3 Know Your Customer (KYC)

3.1 The branch officer collects proof of identity and proof of address from the applicant.

3.2 If both documents are verified, the application proceeds to risk assessment.

3.3 If either document cannot be verified, the application is rejected.

4 Risk assessment

4.1 The branch officer assigns a risk rating of low, medium or high.

4.2 Low-risk applications are approved and the account is opened.

4.3 High-risk applications are referred to the Branch Manager.

4.4 The Branch Manager approves or rejects referred applications within 2 working days.

5 Account opening

5.1 The account must be opened within 3 working days of receiving a complete application.

Definitions

Term | Meaning
Annual leave | Paid leave earned by an employee under the Leave Policy.
Leave balance | The number of annual leave days available to the employee in the HR portal.
Working day | Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays declared by the Bank.

Revision history

Version | Date | Author | Description of change
v1.0 | 01-Apr-2022 | P. Sharma | Initial issue.
v1.1 | 01-Apr-2024 | P. Sharma | Leave requests moved to the HR portal.
v2.0 | 01-Apr-2026 | P. Sharma | Approval bands and decision timelines clarified.

Distribution

The controlled copy of this document is held in the Document Management System (DMS). Printed or downloaded copies are uncontrolled; check the DMS for the current version before use.

1 Purpose

1.1 This procedure describes how employees request and obtain approval for annual leave.

2 Scope

2.1 This procedure applies to all permanent employees.

3 Request

3.1 The employee submits a leave request in the HR portal, stating the start date and the number of working days requested.

3.2 The HR portal checks the employee's leave balance. If the balance is sufficient, the request proceeds to approval.

3.3 If the leave balance is insufficient, the HR portal rejects the request and notifies the employee.

4 Approval

4.1 Requests of 10 working days or fewer are approved or rejected by the employee's line manager.

4.2 Requests of more than 10 working days are approved or rejected by the Head of Department.

4.3 The approver must decide within 2 working days of receiving the request.

5 Outcome

5.1 Approved leave is recorded in the HR portal and the employee is notified.

5.2 Rejected requests are closed and the employee is notified of the reason.

5.3 The employee must be notified of the decision within 3 working days of submitting the request.

Employee Expense Reimbursement Policy

EXP-001 · Version 3.0 · Policy & Procedure

Document control

Document No. | EXP-001 | Version | 3.0
Status | Approved - Effective | Classification | Internal
Effective date | 01-Jul-2026 | Next review date | 30-Jun-2027
Document owner | Chief Financial Officer | Supersedes | v2.0 dated 04-Apr-2024
Department | Finance - Corporate Finance Operations

Review and approval

Role | Name | Designation | Date | Signature
Prepared by | Rohit Menon | Manager - Finance Operations | 12-Jun-2026 | e-signed (DMS)
Reviewed by | Farah Siddiqui | Head - Internal Controls | 18-Jun-2026 | e-signed (DMS)
Approved by | Vikram Iyer | Chief Financial Officer | 24-Jun-2026 | e-signed (DMS)

Definitions

Term | Meaning
Requester | The employee who submits an expense claim for reimbursement.
Line manager | The manager to whom the requester reports, as recorded in the HR system.
Finance Head | The head of the Finance Department (a single position in the company).
Expense portal | The company's online system for submitting and tracking expense claims.

Revision history

Version | Date | Author | Description of change
v1.0 | 12-Mar-2022 | A. Kulkarni | Initial issue.
v2.0 | 04-Apr-2024 | R. Menon | Approval threshold raised from INR 5,000 to INR 10,000; claims moved to the expense portal.
v3.0 | 01-Jul-2026 | R. Menon | Added Audit Committee re-review (Section 6) and the 7-day reimbursement commitment (clause 5.2).

Distribution

The controlled copy of this document is held in the Document Management System (DMS). Printed or downloaded copies are uncontrolled; check the DMS for the current version before use.

1 Purpose

1.1 This policy sets out how employees are reimbursed for business expenses.

2 Scope

2.1 This policy applies to all staff, managers and the Finance Head of the company.

3 Submission

3.1 The requester submits an expense claim with receipts through the expense portal. The Accounts team checks every claim for receipts.

3.2 Claims without receipts are returned to the requester, who must attach the receipts and resubmit; the claim is then checked again.

4 Approval

4.1 Claims below INR 10,000 are approved by the requester's line manager.

4.2 Claims above INR 10,000 require approval from the Finance Head.

4.3 Claims submitted by a manager are approved by the Finance Head.

4.4 The Finance Head's own claims must be approved by the Finance Head.

4.5 Approvers must decide within 3 working days of receiving a claim.

5 Payment

5.1 Approved claims are paid by the Accounts team within 5 working days.

5.2 Every claim must be reimbursed within 7 calendar days of submission.

6 Audit

6.1 Claims escalated by the Audit Committee are re-reviewed by the Internal Audit team before payment.

7 Controls

7.1 No person may approve their own claim.

7.2 Reimbursements must be processed promptly and, where appropriate, in line with company policy.

Employee Expense Reimbursement Policy

EXP-001 · Version 3.0 · Policy & Procedure

Document control

Document No. | EXP-001 | Version | 3.0
Status | Approved - Effective | Classification | Internal
Effective date | 01-Jul-2026 | Next review date | 30-Jun-2027
Document owner | Chief Financial Officer | Supersedes | v2.0 dated 04-Apr-2024
Department | Finance - Corporate Finance Operations

Review and approval

Role | Name | Designation | Date | Signature
Prepared by | Rohit Menon | Manager - Finance Operations | 12-Jun-2026 | e-signed (DMS)
Reviewed by | Farah Siddiqui | Head - Internal Controls | 18-Jun-2026 | e-signed (DMS)
Approved by | Vikram Iyer | Chief Financial Officer | 24-Jun-2026 | e-signed (DMS)

Definitions

Term | Meaning
Requester | The employee who submits an expense claim for reimbursement.
Line manager | The manager to whom the requester reports, as recorded in the HR system.
Finance Head | The head of the Finance Department (a single position in the company).
Expense portal | The company's online system for submitting and tracking expense claims.

Revision history

Version | Date | Author | Description of change
v1.0 | 12-Mar-2022 | A. Kulkarni | Initial issue.
v2.0 | 04-Apr-2024 | R. Menon | Approval threshold raised from INR 5,000 to INR 10,000; claims moved to the expense portal.
v3.0 | 01-Jul-2026 | R. Menon | Added Audit Committee re-review (Section 6) and the 7-day reimbursement commitment (clause 5.2).

Distribution

The controlled copy of this document is held in the Document Management System (DMS). Printed or downloaded copies are uncontrolled; check the DMS for the current version before use.

1 Purpose

1.1 This policy sets out how employees are reimbursed for business expenses.

2 Scope

2.1 This policy applies to all staff, managers and the Finance Head of the company.

3 Submission

3.1 The requester submits an expense claim with receipts through the expense portal. The Accounts team checks every claim for receipts.

3.2 Claims without receipts are returned to the requester, who must attach the receipts and resubmit; the claim is then checked again.

4 Approval

4.1 Claims up to and including INR 10,000 are approved by the requester's line manager.

4.2 Claims above INR 10,000 require approval from the Finance Head.

4.3 Claims submitted by a manager are approved by the Finance Head.

4.4 The Finance Head's own claims must be approved by the Finance Head.

4.5 Approvers must decide within 3 working days of receiving a claim.

5 Payment

5.1 Approved claims are paid by the Accounts team within 5 working days.

5.2 Every claim must be reimbursed within 7 calendar days of submission.

6 Audit

6.1 Claims escalated by the Audit Committee are re-reviewed by the Internal Audit team before payment.

7 Controls

7.1 No person may approve their own claim.

7.2 Reimbursements must be processed promptly and, where appropriate, in line with company policy.

Purchase Requisition and Purchase Order Approval Procedure

PRC-006 · Version 3.0 · Standard Operating Procedure

Document control

Document No. | PRC-006 | Version | 3.0
Status | Approved - Effective | Classification | Internal
Effective date | 01-Apr-2026 | Next review date | 31-Mar-2027
Document owner | Plant Director | Supersedes | v2.3 dated 01-Apr-2025
Department | Procurement

Review and approval

Role | Name | Designation | Date | Signature
Prepared by | Haruka Tanaka | Procurement Section Manager | 05-Mar-2026 | e-signed (DMS)
Reviewed by | Shota Yamamoto | Finance Manager | 12-Mar-2026 | e-signed (DMS)
Approved by | Takeshi Morimoto | Plant Director | 19-Mar-2026 | e-signed (DMS)

Definitions

Term | Meaning
Purchase requisition (PR) | An internal request to buy goods or services, raised in the ERP system.
Purchase order (PO) | The commercial document issued to a supplier to order goods or services.
Approved supplier | A supplier listed in the Approved Supplier List after onboarding and evaluation.
Capital expenditure | Spending on assets with a useful life of more than one year, recorded as fixed assets.

Revision history

Version | Date | Author | Description of change
v2.0 | 01-Apr-2023 | H. Tanaka | Approval matrix introduced.
v2.3 | 01-Apr-2025 | H. Tanaka | Board approval added for requisitions above JPY 50,000,000.
v3.0 | 01-Apr-2026 | H. Tanaka | Section Manager approval limit reduced from JPY 1,000,000 to JPY 500,000 (FY2026 cost-control programme).

Distribution

The controlled copy of this document is held in the Document Management System (DMS). Printed or downloaded copies are uncontrolled; check the DMS for the current version before use.

1 Purpose

1.1 This procedure sets out how goods and services are requisitioned, approved and ordered.

2 Scope

2.1 This procedure applies to all purchases of goods and services by the Nagoya plant, except utilities.

3 Requisition

3.1 The requester raises a purchase requisition in the ERP system with a cost centre and an estimated value.

3.2 The Procurement team checks whether the item is available from an approved supplier.

3.3 If no approved supplier exists, the requisition is sent for supplier onboarding.

4 Approval limits

4.1 Requisitions up to JPY 500,000 are approved by the Section Manager.

4.2 Requisitions above JPY 1,000,000 are approved by the Plant Director.

4.3 Requisitions above JPY 50,000,000 are approved by the Board of Directors.

4.4 Capital expenditure requisitions of any value are approved by the Plant Director.

5 Purchase order

5.1 Once approved, the Procurement team issues a purchase order to the supplier within 2 working days.

5.2 Requisitions rejected by an approver are closed and the requester is notified.

Savings Account Opening Procedure

ACC-002 · Version 1.4 · Standard Operating Procedure

Document control

Document No. | ACC-002 | Version | 1.4
Status | Approved - Effective | Classification | Internal
Effective date | 15-Aug-2026 | Next review date | 14-Aug-2027
Document owner | Head - Retail Banking | Supersedes | v1.3 dated 02-Jan-2026
Department | Retail Banking - Branch Operations

Review and approval

Role | Name | Designation | Date | Signature
Prepared by | Sneha Patil | Manager - Branch Operations | 28-Jul-2026 | e-signed (DMS)
Reviewed by | Arjun Bhatt | Compliance Officer - KYC/AML | 05-Aug-2026 | e-signed (DMS)
Approved by | Meera Nair | Head - Retail Banking | 11-Aug-2026 | e-signed (DMS)

Definitions

Term | Meaning
KYC | Know Your Customer - the process of verifying the identity and address of a customer.
Branch officer | A customer service officer authorised to open accounts at a branch.
Officially valid document | A document accepted by the Bank as proof of identity or address.
Guardian | A parent or court-appointed guardian who operates the account on behalf of a minor.

Revision history

Version | Date | Author | Description of change
v1.0 | 20-Feb-2023 | S. Patil | Initial issue.
v1.3 | 02-Jan-2026 | S. Patil | Risk assessment step introduced (Section 4).
v1.4 | 15-Aug-2026 | S. Patil | Section 9 (Accounts for minors) withdrawn pending regulatory update; account opening timeline added (clause 5.1).

Distribution

The controlled copy of this document is held in the Document Management System (DMS). Printed or downloaded copies are uncontrolled; check the DMS for the current version before use.

1 Purpose

1.1 This procedure describes how a branch opens a savings account for an individual customer.

2 Eligibility

2.1 Applicants must be 18 years of age or older.

2.2 Minors aged below 10 years are not eligible to open an account. Minors aged 10 years and above may open an account jointly with a guardian, as described in Section 9.

3 Know Your Customer (KYC)

3.1 The branch officer collects proof of identity and proof of address from the applicant.

3.2 If both documents are verified, the application proceeds to risk assessment.

3.3 If either document cannot be verified, the application is rejected.

4 Risk assessment

4.1 The branch officer assigns a risk rating of low, medium or high.

4.2 Low-risk applications are approved and the account is opened.

4.3 High-risk applications are referred to the Branch Manager.

4.4 The Branch Manager approves or rejects referred applications within 2 working days.

5 Account opening

5.1 The account must be opened within 3 working days of receiving a complete application.

Pengendalian dokumen

Pemilik dokumen | VP Customer Operations | Menggantikan | v1.2 tanggal 18-Sep-2025

Pemeriksaan dan pengesahan

Peran | Nama | Jabatan | Tanggal | Tanda tangan
Disusun oleh | Dewi Lestari | Disputes Operations Lead | 12-May-2026 | TTE (DMS)
Diperiksa oleh | Bima Prasetyo | Risk & Compliance Manager | 20-May-2026 | TTE (DMS)
Disahkan oleh | Ratna Wijaya | VP Customer Operations | 27-May-2026 | TTE (DMS)

Definisi

Istilah | Pengertian
Sanggahan | Klaim pemegang kartu bahwa suatu transaksi kartu tidak benar, tidak sah, atau tidak sesuai kesepakatan.
Chargeback | Pembatalan transaksi kartu yang dimintakan kepada acquirer melalui prinsipal kartu.
Kredit sementara | Kredit sementara ke rekening nasabah selama sanggahan diselesaikan.
Prinsipal kartu | Jaringan kartu (misalnya GPN, Visa, Mastercard) yang aturannya berlaku atas transaksi.

Riwayat revisi

Versi | Tanggal | Penyusun | Uraian perubahan
v1.0 | 04-Mar-2024 | D. Lestari | Penerbitan awal.
v1.2 | 18-Sep-2025 | D. Lestari | Batas waktu sanggahan diselaraskan menjadi 120 hari.
v2.0 | 01-Jun-2026 | D. Lestari | Penerusan kasus fraud ditambahkan (butir 5.3). Lampiran C (alur investigasi fraud) dipindahkan ke manual Fraud Operations.

Distribusi

Salinan terkendali dokumen ini disimpan dalam Sistem Manajemen Dokumen (DMS). Salinan cetak atau unduhan merupakan salinan tidak terkendali; periksa DMS untuk versi terbaru sebelum digunakan.

1 Tujuan

1.1 Prosedur ini menjelaskan cara sanggahan nasabah atas transaksi kartu diterima, diinvestigasi, dan diselesaikan.

2 Ruang lingkup

2.1 Prosedur ini berlaku untuk sanggahan yang diajukan oleh pemegang kartu ritel atas transaksi kartu debit dan kartu kredit.

3 Penerimaan sanggahan

3.1 Nasabah mengajukan sanggahan melalui aplikasi seluler atau pusat layanan nasabah. Petugas Sanggahan mencatat sanggahan tersebut dalam sistem manajemen kasus.

3.2 Sanggahan yang diajukan lebih dari 120 hari setelah tanggal transaksi ditolak.

3.3 Untuk sanggahan yang diajukan dalam waktu 120 hari, Petugas Sanggahan meminta bukti pendukung dari nasabah.

4 Penelaahan bukti

4.1 Apabila bukti lengkap, sanggahan dilanjutkan ke tahap klasifikasi.

4.2 Apabila bukti tidak lengkap, Petugas Sanggahan mengirimkan pengingat kepada nasabah dan menelaah kembali bukti yang tersedia.

5 Klasifikasi dan penyelesaian

5.1 Sanggahan dengan nilai sampai dengan Rp2.000.000 diselesaikan oleh Petugas Sanggahan dengan memberikan kredit sementara kepada nasabah.

5.2 Sanggahan dengan nilai di atas Rp2.000.000 diteruskan kepada Supervisor Sanggahan.

5.3 Sanggahan yang diklasifikasikan sebagai dugaan penipuan (fraud) diteruskan kepada Unit Investigasi Fraud.

5.4 Supervisor Sanggahan mengajukan chargeback kepada prinsipal kartu atau menolak sanggahan.

5.5 Unit Investigasi Fraud menyelesaikan investigasi sebagaimana diatur dalam Lampiran C.

6 Batas waktu

6.1 Supervisor Sanggahan wajib memberikan keputusan dalam waktu 10 hari kerja sejak sanggahan diteruskan.

6.2 Chargeback diajukan kepada prinsipal kartu dalam waktu 5 hari kerja sejak keputusan Supervisor.

6.3 Setiap sanggahan wajib diselesaikan dalam waktu 14 hari kalender sejak dicatat.

7 Komunikasi dengan nasabah

7.1 Nasabah diberi tahu mengenai hasil penyelesaian sanggahan secara tepat waktu.

Card Transaction Dispute and Chargeback Procedure

DSP-004 · Version 2.0 · Standard Operating Procedure

Document control

Document No. | DSP-004 | Version | 2.0
Status | Approved - Effective | Classification | Internal
Effective date | 01-Jun-2026 | Next review date | 31-May-2027
Document owner | VP Customer Operations | Supersedes | v1.2 dated 18-Sep-2025
Department | Customer Operations - Disputes

Review and approval

Role | Name | Designation | Date | Signature
Prepared by | Dewi Lestari | Disputes Operations Lead | 12-May-2026 | e-signed (DMS)
Reviewed by | Bima Prasetyo | Risk & Compliance Manager | 20-May-2026 | e-signed (DMS)
Approved by | Ratna Wijaya | VP Customer Operations | 27-May-2026 | e-signed (DMS)

Definitions

Term | Meaning
Dispute | A cardholder's claim that a card transaction is incorrect, unauthorised or not as agreed.
Chargeback | A reversal of a card transaction requested from the acquirer through the card scheme.
Provisional credit | A temporary credit to the customer's account while a dispute is resolved.
Card scheme | The card network (e.g. GPN, Visa, Mastercard) whose rules govern the transaction.

Revision history

Version | Date | Author | Description of change
v1.0 | 04-Mar-2024 | D. Lestari | Initial issue.
v1.2 | 18-Sep-2025 | D. Lestari | Dispute window aligned to 120 days.
v2.0 | 01-Jun-2026 | D. Lestari | Fraud referral added (clause 5.3). Annex C (fraud investigation workflow) moved to the Fraud Operations manual.

Distribution

The controlled copy of this document is held in the Document Management System (DMS). Printed or downloaded copies are uncontrolled; check the DMS for the current version before use.

1 Purpose

1.1 This procedure describes how customer disputes on card transactions are received, investigated and resolved.

2 Scope

2.1 This procedure applies to disputes raised by retail cardholders on debit and credit card transactions.

3 Intake

3.1 The customer raises a dispute through the mobile app or the contact centre. The Disputes Officer registers the dispute in the case management system.

3.2 Disputes raised more than 120 days after the transaction date are declined.

3.3 For disputes raised within 120 days, the Disputes Officer requests supporting evidence from the customer.

4 Evidence review

4.1 If the evidence is complete, the dispute proceeds to classification.

4.2 If the evidence is incomplete, the Disputes Officer sends a reminder to the customer and reviews the evidence on file again.

5 Classification and resolution

5.1 Disputes of IDR 2,000,000 or less are resolved by the Disputes Officer with a provisional credit to the customer.

5.2 Disputes above IDR 2,000,000 are referred to the Disputes Supervisor.

5.3 Disputes classified as suspected fraud are referred to the Fraud Investigation Unit.

5.4 The Disputes Supervisor either files a chargeback with the card scheme or declines the dispute.

5.5 The Fraud Investigation Unit completes its investigation as described in Annex C.

6 Timelines

6.1 The Disputes Supervisor must decide within 10 working days of referral.

6.2 Chargebacks are filed with the card scheme within 5 working days of the Supervisor's decision.

6.3 Every dispute must be resolved within 14 calendar days of registration.

7 Customer communication

7.1 The customer is informed of the outcome in a timely manner.

IAM-005 · Version 4.2 · Standard Operating Procedure

Document control

Status | Approved - Effective | Classification | Internal - Restricted
Effective date | 01-Oct-2026 | Next review date | 30-Sep-2027

Review and approval

Role | Name | Designation | Date | Signature
Prepared by | Karan Malhotra | Lead - Identity & Access Management | 10-Sep-2026 | e-signed (DMS)
Reviewed by | Neha Joshi | Information Security Manager | 17-Sep-2026 | e-signed (DMS)
Approved by | Suresh Pillai | Chief Information Officer | 24-Sep-2026 | e-signed (DMS)

Definitions

Term | Meaning
Application owner | The business manager accountable for an application and the data it holds.
Standard access | Access to perform the normal business functions of a role.
Privileged access | Access that allows administration, configuration or bulk change of data or systems.
Recertification | The periodic review in which managers confirm that each user's access is still required.

Revision history

Version | Date | Author | Description of change
v3.0 | 09-Nov-2023 | K. Malhotra | Procedure moved to the IT service portal.
v4.1 | 15-Jan-2026 | K. Malhotra | Contractor approvals assigned to Vendor Management (clause 4.3).
v4.2 | 01-Oct-2026 | K. Malhotra | Emergency access (clause 5.2) added following production incident INC-2291.

Distribution

The controlled copy of this document is held in the Document Management System (DMS). Printed or downloaded copies are uncontrolled; check the DMS for the current version before use.

1 Purpose

1.1 This procedure defines how access to business applications is requested, approved, provisioned and reviewed.

2 Scope

2.1 This procedure applies to employees and contractors who require access to any production application.

3 Request

3.1 The requester's line manager raises an access request in the IT service portal, stating the application and the access level (standard or privileged).

3.2 Requests that do not name an application owner are rejected by the Service Desk.

4 Approval

4.1 Standard access requests are approved by the application owner.

4.2 Privileged access requests are approved by the application owner and then by the Information Security Manager.

4.3 Requests for contractors are approved by the Head of Vendor Management.

4.4 Each approver must decide within 2 working days of receiving the request.

5 Provisioning

5.1 After all required approvals, the IAM team creates the account and grants the approved access within 1 working day.

5.2 In an emergency declared by the Duty Manager, the IAM team may grant privileged access immediately, before any approval is obtained.

5.3 No access may be granted before it has been approved by the application owner.

5.4 Access must be provisioned within 3 working days of the request.

6 Review

6.1 Accounts flagged by the quarterly recertification are revoked by the IAM team.

7 Records

7.1 The IAM team retains approval evidence as appropriate.

Workplace Incident Reporting and Investigation Procedure

INC-007 · Version 1.2 · Standard Operating Procedure

Document control

Document No. | INC-007 | Version | 1.2
Status | Approved - Effective | Classification | Internal
Effective date | 01-Jul-2026 | Next review date | 30-Jun-2027
Document owner | Site HSE Manager | Supersedes | v1.1 dated 01-Jul-2025
Department | Health, Safety & Environment

Review and approval

Role | Name | Designation | Date | Signature
Prepared by | Yui Sato | Site HSE Manager | 08-Jun-2026 | e-signed (DMS)
Reviewed by | Daisuke Ito | Maintenance Supervisor | 15-Jun-2026 | e-signed (DMS)
Approved by | Takeshi Morimoto | Plant Director | 22-Jun-2026 | e-signed (DMS)

Definitions

Term | Meaning
Incident | An unplanned event that resulted in, or could have resulted in, injury, ill health or damage.
Minor incident | An incident requiring no more than first aid and causing no lost time.
Serious incident | An incident causing lost time, medical treatment or significant damage.
Major incident | An incident causing a fatality, permanent disability or a reportable dangerous occurrence.

Revision history

Version | Date | Author | Description of change
v1.0 | 01-Jul-2024 | Y. Sato | Initial issue.
v1.1 | 01-Jul-2025 | Y. Sato | Three-level severity classification introduced.
v1.2 | 01-Jul-2026 | Y. Sato | Independence requirement added (Section 7).

Distribution

The controlled copy of this document is held in the Document Management System (DMS). Printed or downloaded copies are uncontrolled; check the DMS for the current version before use.

1 Purpose

1.1 This procedure ensures that workplace incidents are reported, investigated and corrected so that they do not recur.

2 Scope

2.1 This procedure applies to all employees, contractors and visitors at the Nagoya plant.

3 Reporting

3.1 Any person who is involved in or witnesses an incident reports it to their supervisor as soon as practicable.

3.2 The supervisor records the incident in the HSE system and classifies it as minor, serious or major.

4 Investigation

4.1 Minor incidents are investigated by the area supervisor.

4.2 Serious incidents are investigated by the Site HSE Manager.

4.3 The investigator identifies the root cause and proposes corrective actions.

4.4 The investigation must be completed within 5 working days of the report.

5 Corrective action

5.1 The department head implements the corrective actions within 10 working days of the investigation.

5.2 The Site HSE Manager verifies that the corrective actions are effective and closes the incident.

5.3 Every incident must be closed within 10 working days of being reported.

6 Independence

6.1 No person may investigate an incident that they reported.
